newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Belgrade bourse turnover up in week to February 28.
newsitem.headline: Belgrade bourse turnover up in week to February 28.

text.p: The Belgrade Stock Exchange (BSE) on Monday reported a 40.38 percent rise in turnover in the week ending February 28 with some improvement in the liquidity of the banking sector.
Total BSE turnover rose to 32.148 million dinars ($5.75 million) in 192 transactions from 22.99 million dinars in 185 deals the previous week.
"A certain improvement in banks' liquidity towards the end of last week resulted in increased trade on the bourse," BSE spokesman Milko Stimac told Reuters.
Investors' interest in central bank short-term bonds at an annual interest rate of 88.89 percent was low, with only one five million dinar deal concluded.

"The interest rate on central bank bonds is lower than on other commercial papers and investors obviously chose higher risk for higher interest rather than lack of risk for lower interest," Stimac said.
Trade in wheat forward contracts was also low, with only one deal worth 157,000 dinars concluded.
Lack of investor interest in wheat futures is primarily due to new conditions under which payments can no longer be made in instalments but must be made in full, Stimac said.
For the week ending February 28, the BSE reported the following details:
* Commercial paper accounted for 26.30 million dinars in 183 transactions.
* Treasury bills traded seven times for a volume of 690,000 dinars.
Interest rates on commercial paper and treasury bills ranged from 331 to 520 percent per year, with maturity between six and 30 days.
* Central bank short term bonds were trade in one transaction worth five million dinars at an annual interest rate of 88.89 percent.
* There was only one deal in wheat contracts worth 157,000 dinars.
* OTC trade in commercial paper and treasury bills fell to 24.382 million dinars from 26.857 million a week ago.
* OTC trade in giro money with banks trading their surplus liquidity rose to 20.0 million dinars from 17.648 a week ago.
